entries.note: “Not good enough” judges the revenues' adequacy without a standard.
Neither a “real AI story” nor getting metrics “straight” has a shared test here.

entries.test: Microsoft's AI revenue and GPU allocation disclosures, together with OpenAI's full-year 2026 financial results, would establish the stated shares and loss.
entries.note: The headline combines current shares with a forecast of 2026 losses.

entries.test: Public Azure billing records and Microsoft's Q3 FY2025 AI run rate would establish whether annualized OpenAI inference spending represented approximately 71%.
entries.note: This is a run-rate comparison dependent on the stated quarterly extrapolation.

entries.test: OpenAI's late-2025 Azure inference billing, with the stated exclusions, would establish whether its annualized spending exceeded $18.5 billion.
entries.note: An explicitly labeled numerical estimate remains checkable.

entries.test: Microsoft's customer-level AI revenue and infrastructure utilization records would establish OpenAI's revenue share and whether it consumed a majority of the relevant infrastructure.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies an AI infrastructure context.

entries.test: Microsoft GPU allocation records at publication would establish whether OpenAI occupied at least 80%, allowing for any capacity transferred to Anthropic.
entries.note: He advances 80% as a working estimate; the possibility language concerns the Anthropic caveat.

entries.test: Anthropic's AWS spending and Amazon's contemporaneous AI revenue run rate would establish the asserted doubling, $12 billion annualization, and approximately 80% share.
entries.note: “Will have” estimates a change already achieved, rather than predicting a future increase.

entries.test: Amazon's AI capacity allocation records would establish whether Anthropic occupied more than 75% at publication.
entries.note: “Confident” is a firm commitment under the screening rules.

entries.test: The Dwarkesh interview transcript and the publicly cited evidence supporting Anthropic inference-profitability claims would establish whether those claims rely solely on explicitly non-company examples.
entries.note: The assertion about the evidence supporting profitability claims is stronger than merely questioning profitability.
He presents the causal connection as suggested by timing, rather than established.
No shared threshold distinguishes “real, meaningful demand” or makes these investments incompatible with it.

entries.test: Google's AI capacity and customer allocation disclosures would establish whether Anthropic occupied at least 1.475 GW of the stated 2.95 GW.
entries.note: The proposition faithfully extracts the capacity estimate.

entries.test: Hyperscaler capital expenditure and capacity allocation records, alongside the labs' cash flows and payment obligations, would establish the majority allocations and financing dependence.
entries.note: Public financial disclosures could settle this even if current reporting is incomplete.

entries.test: Industry AI revenue and compute-demand data attributable to OpenAI and Anthropic would establish whether their shares were approximately 70% or higher.
entries.note: The scope is broad, but the numerical market-share assertion is checkable.

entries.test: Public financial and funding records could establish whether the industry's dependence on the labs' continuing fundraising ended without either lab becoming profitable.
entries.note: “This problem” refers specifically to dependence on continued fundraising, not all industry dependence on the labs. The claim asserts profitability as the only remedy.

entries.test: Anthropic's investor representations and contemporaneous financial forecasts would establish whether an $11 billion annual burn projection materially misrepresented its expected losses.
entries.note: The earlier passage makes clear that $11 billion refers to each year. A later forecast miss alone would not establish misleading disclosure.

entries.test: Anthropic's compute contracts, prepayment schedules, construction milestones, and financing cash flows would establish whether the fundraising was required for advance capacity payments.
entries.note: “I'd argue” introduces an asserted explanation, not merely a possibility.
Revenue records could establish an incorrect figure, but “lying” additionally asserts unidentified sources' private knowledge.

entries.test: Anthropic's run-rate methodology and underlying subscription and API revenue records would establish whether calculation choices explain the reported surge.
entries.note: The following paragraphs give concrete content to “peculiar,” including subscription snapshots and prepaid credits.
This caricatures Meta's strategy; losing money is presented sarcastically as a strategic objective.

entries.test: The four companies' financial statements would show whether rising depreciation offsets their operating growth.
entries.note: “Eaten” has a plain financial reading as growth offset by an expense.
“Worth it” supplies no agreed return criterion, margin, or recovery period for the $2 trillion requirement.

entries.test: Realized revenue by customer and the labs' funding sources would establish whether half of the named companies' future revenues came from venture-funded lab payments.
entries.note: The text shifts from backlog to future revenues and inconsistently names companies; the normalization preserves those problems.
The full proposition asserts a private purpose and knowledge of how outsiders will react. Its numerical compute component is independently checkable.

entries.test: AI market revenue data and Amazon's and Microsoft's disclosed AI run rates and cumulative capex would establish the competitive-business assertion and the stated 6% ratios.
entries.note: The numerical comparison is directly checkable despite the looser word “competitive.”

entries.test: The labs' revenue-recognition methods, unit economics, and financial plans would establish whether reported run rates are distorted and whether a financially viable route to profitability exists.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives financial content to the otherwise vague wording.

entries.test: The discussed companies' public AI financial disclosures would establish whether any had demonstrated AI profits by publication.
entries.note: This concerns demonstrated AI profit, not their overall corporate profitability.
“Being tolerated at their current excess” identifies neither an audience nor a measurable outcome for the exclusive causal explanation.
Neither “effectively killing” the product “as they know it” nor invalidating every growth story has an agreed test.
“Realize” asserts private corporate awareness. The underlying customer-revenue dependence is separately checkable.
“Grow tired of it” specifies no observable withdrawal, spending cut, or other decisive outcome.
Being “forced to reckon” specifies no common observable outcome.
“Largest” lacks a shared comparison measure, and positions being impossible to walk back supplies no definite outcome.

entries.test: The labs' cloud contracts, transaction-level revenue and costs, cash flows, and financing records would establish the $718 billion commitments and claimed loss-driven dependence on venture funding.
entries.note: “Every transaction” is a strong universal claim, not merely a claim of aggregate losses.
“It appears” presents a tentative explanation that demand required hyperscaler funding.
